sources.title: K. J. H. Law, A. M. Stuart, and K. C. Zygalakis, Data Assimilation: A Mathematical Introduction
sources.locator: Complete 158-page author manuscript inspected. Chapter 2 §§2.1–2.7: discrete-time data-assimilation, filtering/smoothing, and well-posedness conventions. Chapter 3 §3.3, especially the deterministic and weak-constraint objectives and Theorems 3.10/3.12: 4DVAR objectives, MAP interpretation, and multiple-minimum warning. Chapter 4 §4.2.1, equations (4.14a–c): fixed-covariance 3DVAR update. Chapter 4 §4.2.3: perturbed-observation EnKF, sample covariance/gain/update, large-ensemble linear-Gaussian statement, and nonlinear approximation caveat. Chapter 4 §4.4.2, Theorem 4.10 and complete proof: contraction tracking bound.

contents.name: Forecast, analysis, filtering, and smoothing terminology
contents.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.1–2.7; finite-horizon state and data-indexed conditional-law scope.
contents.reason: The item fixes finite-dimensional notation and explicitly distinguishes predictive/filtering laws from fixed-interval smoothing and point analysis.

contents.name: Fixed-covariance 3DVAR objective and gain update
contents.locator: Chapter 4 §4.2.1, equations (4.14a–c); the minimizer identity is proved locally.
contents.reason: The source supplies the fixed covariance, innovation, gain, and mean recursion. The local theorem proves the SPD solve, unique quadratic minimizer, MAP identity, and Kalman correspondence.

contents.name: Strong- and weak-constraint 4DVAR objectives and optimization boundary
contents.locator: Chapter 3 §3.3, deterministic objective (3.8), weak-constraint objective, and Theorems 3.10/3.12; the source explicitly leaves numerical optimization methods outside its result.
contents.reason: The algorithm defines both trajectory objectives and a finite gradient run, without importing a convergence claim.

contents.name: Perturbed-observation EnKF variant and nonlinear limitation
contents.locator: Chapter 4 §4.2.3, equations (4.15–4.17) and accompanying large-ensemble and nonlinear-limit discussion.
contents.reason: The source distinguishes the perturbed-observation procedure from deterministic square-root variants and states the nonlinear approximation boundary.

contents.name: 3DVAR Gaussian MAP update
contents.locator: Chapter 4 §§4.1–4.2.1; Bayes/precision update leading to (4.14).
contents.reason: The source motivates the quadratic as a Gaussian MAP update; the complete normal-equation and density argument is written locally.

contents.name: 3DVAR truth-tracking estimate
contents.locator: Chapter 4 §4.4.2, Theorem 4.10 and its full proof.
contents.reason: The source recurrence is reproduced with the induced error norm constant explicit, and the geometric-series argument is complete locally.

contents.name: EnKF linear-Gaussian ensemble-size limit and nonlinear boundary
contents.locator: Chapter 4 §4.2.3 and concluding discussion: the linear Kalman limit is in ensemble size; nonlinear posterior convergence is not asserted.
contents.reason: The item proves a fixed-horizon limit locally, using the independently read convergence article for route confirmation; it does not transfer the linear theorem to nonlinear models.

The HTML chapter bodies and displayed derivations were inspected.

contents.name: State/data assimilation setup and MAP cost
contents.locator: Chapters 2–3, especially Chapter 3 §3.1 equations (3.1–3.4) and Gaussian cost discussion.
contents.reason: Independent textbook treatment supports the forecast/analysis vocabulary and the interpretation of a Gaussian quadratic objective.

contents.name: 3DVAR cost function and analysis update
contents.locator: Chapter 6 §6.2, equation (6.17), plus Chapter 3 MAP gradient/normal-equation discussion.
contents.reason: The source states the covariance-weighted background and data-misfit objective; the local argument proves its unique solution.

contents.name: Strong- and weak-constraint 4DVAR
contents.locator: Chapters 4 §4.1 and 5 §§5.1–5.2; deterministic trajectories are optimized in strong mode and model errors are penalized in weak mode.
contents.reason: The distinct trajectory variables and objective terms are stated explicitly; no convergence guarantee is imported.

contents.name: Ensemble covariance and ensemble-filter methods
contents.locator: Chapter 8 §§8.2–8.8, anomaly/covariance and perturbed-measurement formulas; Chapter 6 relates ensemble methods to the Kalman/3DVAR update.
contents.reason: This independent treatment confirms that ensemble covariance conventions and stochastic perturbation choices are part of the algorithm specification.

contents.name: Finite-ensemble and nonlinear examples
contents.locator: Chapters 6 and 8, 3DVar and ensemble covariance examples and limitations.
contents.reason: The example supplies its own exact positive-probability witness; the source provides the finite-ensemble context.

contents.name: 4DVAR local-minimum boundary

contents.reason: The local polynomial objective and both minima are verified directly.

alternatives.argument: Definition-only item: the carrier directly fixes finite-horizon Euclidean model and observation maps, requires their Borel measurability, and states the forecast, analysis, predictive, filtering, and fixed-interval smoothing conventions; it asserts no additional theorem beyond the cited conditional-kernel suppliers.

Definition-only procedure: for B, Gamma positive definite, S=HBH^T+Gamma satisfies z^T S z=(H^Tz)^T B(H^Tz)+z^T Gamma z>0; Cholesky therefore exists, the triangular solves define K, and the stated mean update is a finite point-estimate procedure.

Definition-only procedure: the strong objective penalizes the initial background and observation residuals along the deterministic model path; the weak objective adds positive-definite model-error penalties on the full path. The selected objective is differentiated and a finite gradient-descent run returns its last iterate; no convergence claim is made.

Definition-only procedure: the empirical C_zz is positive semidefinite as a sum of outer products, so S_N=C_zz+Gamma is positive definite. Cholesky and triangular solves define the common gain; the explicitly independent Gaussian perturbations then define each member update.

Complete local verification in items/ex-finite-ensemble-covariance-fluctuation.md: C_2=(X_1-X_2)^2/4; the independent positive-density event -0.1<X_1<0.1 and 3<X_2<3.1 forces C_2>2.1025>1, whereas Var(N(0,1))=1. Its exact dependencies are listed below.

Complete local verification in items/ex-four-dimensional-variational-objective-has-two-local-minima.md: J(u)=1/2-u^2+u^4/2, J'(u)=u(2u^2-1), and the only stationary points are 0 and +/-1/sqrt(2). The latter two are strict local minima with value 1/8; coercivity and J(0)=1/2 show both are global minimizers, so uniqueness fails. Its exact dependencies are listed below.
